concepts.def: Holidays: where you go, how you travel and what you do, a key part of the international-world topic.
Tourism and travel abroad, including booking accommodation and visiting attractions in other countries.
French-speaking countries around the world, such as Canada, Senegal and Belgium, where French is spoken.
Festivals and celebrations in different countries, broadening cultural understanding of the wider world.
Global warming, a worldwide issue discussed when considering our place in the international community.
Volunteering, including helping abroad or on global causes, linking personal action to international issues.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area E: The International World — a core area of GCSE French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area E: The International World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area E: The International World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
